answer: Require each identity to hold a sealed replica of a public dataset, encoded with its own key so that copies cannot be shared between accounts. Random audits ask for one chunk, say a survey record of violet lotus beds on a small island, with a deadline too short to re-encode the data on demand. Running a thousand identities then means paying to store a thousand full replicas, so the cost grows with account count and cannot be pooled, while an honest agent pays for only one.
